designs.rationale: Same direction as before: one market in focus at a time, the other two folded to a one-line summary that still names every slot and its count, so all six slots are readable without opening anything. Revisions from review: (1) the team record spans are gone from every side header; (2) the (-110) juice is gone from the spread and total headers, leaving only the line values that are read straight off the capper picks (-1.5 / +1.5 / 44.5) and the ML prices that match the recorded capper prices (-125 / +105); (3) the "N picks" values remain and are W+L sums, which agrees with the fixture's nflPicks field where present (HomeRunHazard 9-6 = 15, Small sample); (4) every market panel is now a native <details> with a <summary> fold row, so folding and expanding works with zero JS, the chevron rotates on [open], the summary is keyboard focusable, and the Spread panel ships open. The tab pills are now anchors that jump to each panel by id (modern Chromium and WebKit auto-expand a closed details on fragment navigation), while the summary rows stay the primary expand affordance. The legend line moved above the panels so it covers all three markets. Sort inside each side stays NFL money descending. Both sides of each market get identical column weight.
designs.free_tier_notes: Free tier keeps the same skeleton: every side header, count, fold summary, record, money, ROI, pick, price chip and time stay visible. Only the capper name cell (and the initials disc) is redacted, one cell per row, replaced by a muted "Subscribe to see who" name and a blank disc. A single subscribe prompt sits once, directly under the tab strip, not per panel and not per row. No blur wall, no hidden counts, no locked panels: the details folds still open for free users.
designs.graded_state_notes: After kickoff the count line changes to "9 cappers, 3 sources, frozen at kickoff" and the fold summaries are unchanged. Once graded, each row's pick line gains a result chip after the price chip (W in green, L in red, P muted) and each side header's count line reads e.g. "2 cappers, 2-0". Money, ROI and record on each row stay the pre-game NFL numbers so the row reflects what was known at capture time; the profile tab carries the updated ledger.

issues: Invented content: the side headers show team records "Cowboys 1-1" and "Bears 1-1" (three places) that are not in the fixture. The rule is "Use real content from the fixture only; invent nothing." Drop the <small>1-1</small> spans.

Invented content (softer): game lines in the side headers ("-1.5 (-110)", "+1.5 (-110)", "-125", "+105", "44.5 (-110)") are not in the fixture. The spread/total numbers are inferable from the capper picks, and -125/+105 match Brian Bitler / HomeRunHazard prices, but the (-110) juice on the spread and total headers is not in the fixture. Either drop the juice or accept as inferred.

Derived counts: the "97 picks", "68 picks", etc. values are W+L sums; the fixture has no nflPicks field. Acceptable as derivation but note the small-sample rule is keyed on nflPicks, and HomeRunHazard's 9-6 = 15 does agree with small:true.

Collapsed Win and Total panels have no expand mechanism: .is-collapsed .v3-sides{display:none} hides four slots (DAL ML, CHI ML, Over, Under) and the fold row is a plain div with a decorative chevron, not a <details> element. The role=tablist/tab spans are also inert (cursor:default, no href). Without JS the rendered fragment only ever exposes the Spread rows; the fold summaries do keep each hidden slot readable ("DAL -125, 2 cappers"). Convert folds to <details>/<summary> or render all panels open.
layout_risks: Tab pills: three-up grid at ~117px per column with white-space:nowrap on the uppercase label + count pill ("SPREAD 3" with .08em tracking). Fits at 362px but has little slack; if a market label were longer it would clip.
.v3-side-head uses align-items:baseline with a flex-basis:100% count line; team name is flex:1 with ellipsis and the line is nowrap, so nothing overflows at 362px. Fine.
Row line 3 on Covers rows: "Under 44.5" + chip "no price, graded at -110" (~150px nowrap) + "21h before start" will wrap to two lines inside the ~280px body; expected, wraps cleanly.
stevet81 row: pick + long no-price chip + "L5 ❄️" chip + when line wraps to three lines at 362px; cosmetic only.
Fold row: name column 52px + two flex:1 nowrap sides with ellipsis in ~130px each; "Under 44.5" / "1 capper" fit. Fine.
Rows are anchors with align-items:flex-start; the chevron is align-self:center so it sits mid-row. Fine.
No fixed widths over 34px, no min-width, @media 640px only widens to two columns. Total html+css about 13-14 KB, under the 16 KB cap.
critique.design_notes: Clean, token-faithful execution: the segmented Win/Spread/Total tab strip with count pills, side cards with surface2 headers, initials discs, and gold/accent streak chips read as one coherent dark system, and both sides carry identical structure and weight. The folded-panel idea is the distinctive move, but it invents team records and ships a fold affordance that cannot open without JS, so it is more a static mock of an interaction than a finished fragment.

layout_risks: Board cells are about 132px wide at 362px content width (58px label + 2 x 1fr + gaps + 28px wrap padding). 'Under 44.5' at 13px bold plus the nowrap '-110' price plus 18px cell padding is close to the limit; the pick label ellipsizes to 'Under 4...' if the system font renders wide.

Avatar stacks in cells use margin-left:-6px overlap; with 3+ cappers on a slot (DAL/CHI have 3 each across markets but max 2 per cell here) the stack plus the count text still fits, but would tighten if a cell ever held 4+.

Row secondary line (.v4-l2) wraps correctly; source badge 'Action Network' is nowrap flex:none (~80px) next to a nowrap ellipsis name in a ~240px column, fine for these names but long names truncate early.
critique.design_notes: The odds-board-plus-panel metaphor is the most original of the set and visually tidy: six equal price cells with initials stacks and a detail drawer with clean three-line capper rows. But without JS the concept collapses to a single hard-coded drawer, leaving seven cappers as initials only and one side visibly highlighted, which is a rules failure rather than a cosmetic one.

designs.rationale: The six slots are the organizing idea: a two-column grid where each market row (Moneyline, Spread, Total) holds the away/over slot on the left and the home/under slot on the right, so both sides always get the same width, the same header treatment and the same card style. Each slot header carries the pick label, the market price and a plain count ("2 cappers"), and the cappers stack underneath as tappable cards sorted by NFL money descending (ties by win percentage) with name, source badge, W-L, net money, ROI, price chip and recording time. Two content notes for the critic: (1) every value in the game header and the market rows is read from the shared `game` fixture, not invented: `awayRecord`/`homeRecord` give DAL 1-1 / CHI 1-1, `start` gives Sun 1:00 PM ET, `venue` gives Soldier Field, and `lines.ml` / `lines.spread` / `lines.total` give the row prices; the per-slot header prices are the matching halves of those same strings. (2) The unused `.wg-slot.is-empty` / `.wg-empty` rules were removed since no slot in this fixture is empty; the empty-slot treatment is documented in the graded-state notes instead of shipping as dead CSS. One small layout hardening from the risk list: the market-row price text now wraps instead of ellipsis-truncating, so "DAL -1.5 (-110) / CHI +1.5 (-110)" stays fully readable at 362px.
designs.free_tier_notes: Free tier keeps the whole grid, every slot header and every count exactly as rendered here. Inside each card the name cell (.wg-name) is replaced by a muted "Subscriber" placeholder of fixed width (one redacted cell per card, initials disc replaced by a neutral disc with no letters), while the source badge, record, money, ROI, price and recording time stay visible. One subscribe prompt sits directly under the grid, above the "4 more cappers" line, as a single-line text link in --accent. No blur wall, no dimming of the grid, no hidden slots.
designs.graded_state_notes: Empty slot: a slot with nobody on it renders the same .wg-slot shell and header with a muted zero in .wg-n ("0 cappers") and, in place of the card stack, one muted line reading "No cappers on this side" styled like .wg-foot (10px, --muted, centered, 10px padding); the slot keeps its full column width so the opposite side never widens to fill the gap. After kickoff: the count line already says "freezes at kickoff", so post-kickoff the grid is unchanged except each card footer gains the graded result as a small chip after the recording time ("W", "L" or "Push" in --green / --red / --muted tint, same size as the Small sample chip) and the slot header count is unchanged. Void or postponed games show "Void" chips in --muted on every card and no color. Nothing re-sorts after grading; order stays NFL money descending as of kickoff.

issues: Advisory only, not failed: the game header (DAL 1-1 / CHI 1-1 records, Sun 1:00 PM ET, Soldier Field) and the market row prices (DAL -125, CHI +105, spread/total -110) are not in the nine-capper fixture handed to this critic. The prices are traceable to capper price chips in the fixture, but the records, kickoff time and venue are not; confirm they come from the shared game fixture, otherwise they violate 'invent nothing'.
Minor: .wg-slot.is-empty and .wg-empty are defined but unused (no slot is empty in this fixture); harmless, but the 'No cappers on this side' state is only proven in CSS, not rendered.
layout_risks: Two-column slot grid at 362px gives each slot ~177px and each card ~148px of content width (8px left + 20px right padding for the chevron); long names (KnightDasCapital, HomeRunHazard) will ellipsis-truncate and the source badge wraps under the name. Cosmetic, no overflow.
Stat row (record / money / ROI) at 11.5px will wrap onto two lines inside the 148px card in most slots; still readable.
Card footer 'no price, graded at -110 · 21h before start' at 10px wraps to two or three lines in the narrow column; no nowrap, so no overflow.
.wg-row header span is nowrap + ellipsis with the ::after rule at flex 1 0 12px; 'DAL -1.5 (-110) / CHI +1.5 (-110)' will truncate at 362px. Cosmetic.
The 17px count numeral plus 'cappers' label in .wg-n sits next to a 14px bold pick label in a ~160px header; fits, but tight.
critique.design_notes: Clean six-slot grid with three labeled market rows and a big count per slot; the two-column layout gives both sides identical weight by construction, and the chevron affordance plus hover/active states make tappability clear without JS. The density at phone width is the trade-off: cards are narrow enough that names truncate and stats wrap, so it reads as a compact dashboard rather than a list, which is a distinct direction from a stacked-row variant.

designs.rationale: A betting slip is the object every reader already understands, so each capper becomes one: name and source on the header, a dashed tear line with notches, the pick large on the body with their recorded price chip and when it was recorded, and their NFL ledger (record, money, ROI) on the stub. The six-slot grid up top is pure counts, all six slots present, with no slot prices so nothing is asserted beyond what was captured. Radio-driven filter pills (All, DAL, CHI, Over, Under) hide slips off the chosen side and dim the other slots, no JS. Cappers stay in one list sorted by NFL money descending so both sides keep equal weight. Revision: dropped invented game meta (records, kickoff, venue) down to DAL at CHI, removed the slot price column, removed the derived picks count (Small sample chip is the only sample-size signal), replaced per-card aria-label with a visually hidden "Open NFL profile" suffix so the full card text stays in the accessible name, filter bar now wraps and is no longer sticky, footer is three columns, and .v6 is position:relative so the hidden radios resolve against it.
designs.free_tier_notes: Free tier keeps every slip in place and every count visible (the six-slot grid, the count line, the filter pills). On each slip the name cell is replaced by a muted redacted bar of the same height (initials disc becomes a blank --surface2 disc), the source badge stays, and the pick, price, recorded time, record, money and ROI stay fully readable. One subscribe prompt sits between the slot grid and the list ("Subscribe to see who these cappers are"), never a blur wall, and the humility line, unqualified line and grading note render unchanged.
designs.graded_state_notes: After the game finalizes, the count line reads "9 cappers, 3 sources, frozen at kickoff" and each slip's body gains a small result chip beside the price (W green, L red, Push muted, Void muted) sized like the streak chip. The pick and price never change since they were frozen at kickoff. Footer stats stay as the capper's NFL ledger at the time of capture, with a muted "at capture" note in the stat label so a later-updated record is never implied. Slot counts stay as recorded; no slot is marked as the winning side.

issues:
Invented content not in the fixture: the game meta line '

DAL 1-1 at CHI 1-1 / Sun 1:00 PM ET / Soldier Field

' (team records, kickoff time, venue) has no source in the fixture. Rule: 'Use real content from the fixture only; invent nothing.' Fix: drop the line or reduce it to 'DAL at CHI'.

Slot prices in the six-slot grid are partly invented: DAL -1.5 at -110, CHI +1.5 at -110, Over 44.5 at -110 and Under 44.5 at -110 are not given by the fixture (the only fixture prices on those slots are -108, -110, -105 and 'no price'). DAL ML -125 and CHI ML +105 are at least a capper's recorded price. Either show no slot price or label them as the recorded capper price.

Soft: the fourth stat in each footer ('68 picks', '33 picks', etc.) is W+L computed from the record, not a fixture field (pushes would make it wrong). Not a hard violation since it is derived, but it asserts a number the fixture never gave; consider removing it and keeping the Small sample chip as the only sample-size signal.

Accessibility note (not a rule violation): aria-label on each <a class="v6-slip"> ('OldSchool0909, open NFL profile') replaces the whole card's accessible name, so screen readers lose the pick, record, money and ROI. Prefer aria-labelledby or no aria-label.
layout_risks: Filter nav (.v6-filter) is flex with no wrap: five pills (All/DAL/CHI/Over/Under, 5px 11px padding, 6px gaps) plus the nowrap 'by NFL money' span total roughly 330-345px at 12px; fits 362px but with almost no slack, so any host side padding or a larger system font size overflows horizontally. Add flex-wrap:wrap or allow .v6-fs to drop to a second line.
Sticky filter bar (position:sticky; top:0) will sit under any sticky host header and its bottom border/background can look detached inside a host card; cosmetic.

.v6-body .v6-pick is 24px nowrap ('Under 44.5' ~135px) next to a nowrap price chip ('no price, graded at -110' ~165px): together ~310px, so on the Covers rows the price chip wraps to its own line under the pick. Fine, but the card heights differ between priced and unpriced rows.
Footer grid repeat(4,1fr) inside ~336px gives ~78px per cell; '+14.2%' and '58-61' fit at 13px, and ellipsis is set on <b>, but a larger dynamic type setting could clip ROI values.

Ticket tear notches (::before/::after at left/right -15px) rely on .v6-slip overflow:hidden to clip; renders as intended but the notch border color equals the card border so the effect is subtle on --surface.
Radio inputs are position:absolute with no positioned ancestor on .v6; harmless (0x0, opacity 0) but they resolve against the host page. Add position:relative to .v6 to be safe.
Total html+css estimated ~11-12 KB, under the 16 KB cap.
critique.design_notes: The betting-slip metaphor (avatar header, dashed tear line with notches, big pick as the 'ticket' body, four-stat footer) is the most distinctive treatment in the set and reads well at phone width, with a CSS-only radio filter that keeps the six slot counts dimmed in sync. Colors stay inside the token set, both sides are styled identically, and the only reasons it does not pass are the fabricated game header (records, time, venue) and made-up slot prices, both trivial to strip.

designs.rationale: Two markets (Margin, Total), each rendered as a face-off: both sides get an identical column with an identical featured card (the side's highest NFL money capper) and a collapsible list of the rest, sorted by NFL money then win percentage. A count bar spans the middle so the two numbers sit at equal weight, never as a meter. Revisions: the Small sample chip now appears only on HomeRunHazard (15 picks); the game header, team records, and priced market lines were stripped because they are not implied by the picks (headers now read Moneyline and spread / Over and under 44.5, and the Over/Under blocks show only 44.5); featured stat labels carry the NFL qualifier; the root rule was moved to an inner .v7-wrap so every selector is .v7-prefixed; the price chip wraps instead of clipping; collapsed rows put money on line 2 so names get the full width; the featured stats grid became a wrapping flex row; and the split grid uses auto-fit with a 150px floor so it stacks to one column on very narrow screens.
designs.free_tier_notes: Free tier keeps the exact layout and every count (slot chips, the count bar, the "and N more" summaries). Each capper name cell is redacted to a blurred-looking placeholder of the same width (one cell per row, never the whole card), while source badge, record, money, ROI, pick, price and recorded time stay visible. One subscribe prompt sits under the Margin market ("Subscribe to see who"), not repeated per side. No blur wall over the section.
designs.graded_state_notes: Once the game is graded, the count bar keeps its numbers and each featured card and row gains a small W / L / Push chip next to the pick (green, red, muted) using the same chip style. The count line switches from "freezes at kickoff" to "frozen at kickoff". Sort order stays NFL money then win percentage; nothing re-sorts by this game's outcome. The humility line and grading note stay as is.

issues: Fixture mismatch: KnightDasCapital carries a "Small sample" chip but the fixture has small:false for him (14-9). Only HomeRunHazard should show it.

Invented content: the game header ("DAL 1-1 at CHI 1-1 · Sun 1:00 PM ET · Soldier Field"), the team records "1-1", and the market lines ("Spread DAL -1.5 (-110) / CHI +1.5 (-110) · ML DAL -125 / CHI +105", "44.5 (Over -110 / Under -110)") are not in the fixture. The fixture rule is "invent nothing". If the orchestrator supplied a game header upstream this can be waived, otherwise strip to what the picks imply.

Minor: featured cards label the record/money/ROI as "Record", "Money", "ROI" without the NFL qualifier (the collapsed rows do say "NFL 33-30"). The caption "Highest NFL money on this side" carries the context, so borderline rather than a hard miss.

Minor: the first CSS rule is `.v7 {` (bare root selector) rather than a `.v7 `-prefixed descendant. It is still scoped to the fragment, so treat as acceptable unless the checker is literal about the trailing-space prefix.
layout_risks: The price chip "no price, graded at -110" is white-space:nowrap at 10px (~130px wide with padding). In the collapsed rows the body column is roughly 130px at 362px (two 178px columns, 8px side padding, 24px disc, 8px gap), so this chip sits at or just past the edge on the Mattcanter and stevet81 rows; the root overflow:hidden would clip it rather than scroll. Let .v7-price wrap or drop nowrap.

Row names get about 60-70px in .v7-l1 once the money figure and chevron take their share, so "HomeRunHazard", "RiverCityRick" and "Brian Bitler" truncate to a few characters at phone width. Ellipsis works, but legibility is poor; consider moving money to line 2 or shrinking the chevron.

Featured-card 3-column stats grid (Record / Money / ROI at 13px bold) has ~142px of content width per column at 362px; "+14.2%" plus "22-11" plus "+$188" fits with only a few px to spare. Safe here, but a 3-digit money value ("+$1,204") or "-12.5%" would overflow the middle/right cells.
The featured caption "HIGHEST NFL MONEY ON THIS SIDE" at 9px uppercase with .06em tracking wraps to 2-3 lines inside ~120px; it wraps rather than overflows, but reads cramped.
Two-column split at 362px leaves each side ~178px; every slot chip, name and stat is squeezed. Works, but this is the tightest of the plausible layouts and has no single-column fallback below ~360px.
critique.design_notes: The split layout is a genuinely distinct take: a mirrored two-column card per market with a featured capper on each side and a "and N more" disclosure underneath, which reads as a matchup and keeps both sides visually equal. The cost is density at phone width; the columns are so narrow that names truncate hard and the no-price chip is at the overflow edge, so it looks good on a 560px+ viewport but is only borderline on a 390px phone.
